title: dns(save.sh): encrypting the tfstate of record is not atomic — a failed sops -e truncates terraform.tfstate.enc to zero bytes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Problem

`infra/dns/save.sh` writes the encrypted Terraform state of record non-atomically: `sops -e … > terraform.tfstate.enc` (save.sh:50). The shell truncates `terraform.tfstate.enc` **before** `sops` runs, so any encryption failure — missing/expired sops key, sops error, disk full, interruption — leaves the state of record empty or partial, destroying the only encrypted copy the whole DNS workflow treats as canonical.

This is the one unguarded write left in the flow the #1943 campaign hardened: `load.sh` refuses a missing/empty `.enc`, `init.sh` snapshots and byte-verifies the decrypted state around `tofu init`, and `plan.sh` re-verifies lineage and sets `SKIP_SAVE` on its refusal paths so the EXIT trap cannot save a refused state. But `save.sh` itself — including when `plan.sh`'s EXIT-trap cleanup invokes it after a successful plan — can still zero the record on a routine sops failure.

## Evidence

`infra/dns/save.sh` @ `2bcd46e0dc`:

- :44-47 the already-current fast path decrypts and compares first, so the destructive path is only reached when the state actually changed — exactly when the new ciphertext matters most.
- :50 `sops -e "$dir/terraform.tfstate" >"$dir/terraform.tfstate.enc"` — in-place redirection, no temp file, no rename, no post-write verification (contrast `init.sh`'s snapshot + sha256 verify + restore).
- `set -Eexuo pipefail` (save.sh:2) makes the script exit on the sops failure, but the truncation has already happened; nothing restores the previous ciphertext.

Verified this run on the laptop (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-dns-save`, real `save.sh` copied verbatim, stub `sops` on PATH):

- Stub `sops -d` returns differing content (so the already-current fast path is skipped); stub `sops -e` exits 1: `save.sh` exits 1 and `terraform.tfstate.enc` goes from 26 bytes to **0 bytes**.
- Control (stub `sops -e` succeeds): exit 0, `.enc` holds the new ciphertext (15 bytes).

## Why it matters

`terraform.tfstate.enc` is the state of record for the DNS estate: `load.sh` decrypts it, `init.sh` calls it "the decrypted state of record" and refuses to continue without it, and a void/mismatched state is the #1943 failure mode ("151 to add, 0 to destroy" against an empty state). Losing it to a transient sops failure turns a retry-able error into state recovery from the plaintext working copy — if that copy has been cleaned (`cleanup_terraform_tfstate.sh` exists in the same directory) or the failure happens on another machine, the encrypted record is simply gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `save.sh` encrypts to a temporary file in the same directory and atomically renames it over `terraform.tfstate.enc` only after `sops` exits 0 (and the temp file is non-empty); a failed encryption leaves the previous `.enc` byte-identical.
- [ ] A post-write sanity check (e.g. the new `.enc` decrypts and its lineage matches the plaintext state, mirroring plan.sh's check) runs before the save is reported successful, or the rename only happens after such a check on the temp file.
- [ ] The temp file is cleaned up on failure without touching the live `.enc`; the `.lock` cleanup behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] A test/probe with a failing `sops -e` stub shows `.enc` unchanged and a non-zero exit; a succeeding stub shows the new ciphertext in place; the already-current fast path still skips re-encryption.
- [ ] `load.sh`'s analogous in-place decrypt write (`sops -d … > terraform.tfstate`, load.sh:41) is assessed in the same pass: the plaintext target is re-derivable from `.enc`, so it may be documented as safe-by-reconstruction rather than changed — but the reasoning is recorded on this issue.
